messages.subject: conceptual question-multilevel regression
parts:
Hello All

I am using STAN for a multilevel hierarchial bayesian regression model. I have two 'levels'- say 'items' and 'Product_category' . There are many transactions within a item type and there are may items within a 'Product_category'.  There are 3 predictors in my input matrix. Usually, the model works well with the data. However, there are some (rare) cases where the item type has the same value throughout for one of the predictors (as in the 'size' property of the transactions is 100 metres throughout). In ths case the beta(posterior distribution corresponding to size) is wrongly calculated in absence of any variation in my predictor.This is ofcourse kind of expected-however I believed that the whole point of using a hierarchial bayesian model is that the model will 'draw' information from the level-2 of the hierarchy and hence there will be  constraint to what values beta can take. This isnt happenning. Pretty sure I am doing something remarkably stupid---so any help is appreciated on this :)

Thanks and Regards

messages.author: 8aa9b8cc06fdc99c
messages.subject: Re: [stan-users] conceptual question-multilevel regression

I'm not sure what beta(posterior distribution corresponding to size)
is and how you're determining what the right value is.

Also, we can't offer much help without seeing your model.

parts:
Your hierarchical model doesn't have a hierarchical variance component.
That's what would control posterior variance. Instead, you've
hardcoded the value 10.

Also, it looks like the pooling is backwards. You have:

> for (j in 1:J)
> a[j]~ normal(0, sigma_a);

> for (j in 1:J)
> beta[j] ~ normal((u[j] * gamma), 10);
>
> for (n in 1:N) {

> y_hat[n] <- a[condolist[n]] +beta[condolist[n]][1] * x[n,1] +beta[condolist[n]][2] * x[n,2] +beta[condolist[n]][3] * x[n,3];


The prior for a looks OK (though it should be vectorized),
but you're pooling the parameters for each group beta[j,] rather than
pooling across groups, than beta[,1], beta[,2], and beta[,3].

- Bob

parts:
> On Oct 14, 2015, at 8:19 PM, UD1989 <upasa...@gmail.com> wrote:
>
> U(j) is the matrix group level predictors. For example on the radon example commonly used it would be the county level uranium levels matrix.
> Beta=gamma * u i.e theres a linear relationship. J is number of groups in the hierarchy
> I tried writing it without the j as
> Col(beta,k)~normal(u*gamma,sigma-beta); but there's an expected dimensionality mismatch since col(beta,k) is a vector and the right side is not.
> Beta needs to be expressed suitably as a function of u, and its frustrating that I'm unable to write this simple thing...

Would you mind sending the current model you're working on
and the error message you're getting?

You can't do col(beta, k) here because beta isn't a matrix,
it's an array of vectors.
vector [M] beta[J]; //indiv. coeff by group

But assuming you make it a (J x M) matrix, then col(beta, m)
will be a size J column vector.
matrix[J, L] u; //group predictors
matrix[L,M] gamma; //group coeff

But then (u * gamma) is going to be a (J x M) matrix, so I'm not
quite sure what your intent is here. But we definitely don't allow
matrices in the first argument position of a normal.

And then I don't see a sigma in the last model I found.

- Bob

messages.subject: Re: [stan-users] conceptual question-multilevel regression
parts:
Did this model work OK? It looks the right way around to
me in terms of the hierarchical model in that you're pooling
across the j in each column of beta.

You can vectorize this:

for (j in 1:J)
a[j]~ normal(0, sigma_a);

as just

a ~ normal(0, sigma_a);

And you should be able to replace all those loops in mu_beta
with a single matrix multiply:

mu_beta <- u * gamma;

As usual, don't trust my matrix algebra without confirming it
yourself!

messages.subject: Re: [stan-users] conceptual question-multilevel regression
parts:
Hi Bob!

Thanks a lot for patiently trying to help me!!! :) The final model i used is pasted below. The main issue was happenning because I did not grasp this nugget of information: "If tmp is declared as a matrix then tmp[i] will access the ith row. But if tmp is declared as an array of column vectors then tmp[i] will access the ith column vector. " (someone answered this on another thread.)

The model seems to work fine on a small datset of about 500 observations-currently the model is running on my full datset and I expect it to take a couple of days.
Thanks again for your help!!

library(rstan)
Pred.data <- c("N", "J", "M", "L", "y", "x", "u", "condolist")
stanmodelcode<-"
data {
int<lower=0> N;
int<lower=0> J;
vector[N] y;

int<lower=0> M;
int<lower=0> L;
matrix[N, M] x;
matrix[J, L] u;
int <lower=1,upper=J> condolist[N]; 

}
parameters {
real a[J]; 

//vector[M] beta[J];   //array of vectors eqv to matrix[M,J]
matrix[M,J] beta;
matrix[L,M] gamma;

real<lower=0> sigma_y;
real<lower=0> sigma_a;
vector[M] sigma_beta;

}

model {
vector[N] y_hat;


to_vector(gamma) ~ normal(0,10);

sigma_a ~ cauchy(0,2.5);

for (j in 1:J)
a[j]~ normal(0, sigma_a);
for (k in 1:M)

row(beta,k) ~ normal(u* col(gamma,k) , sigma_beta[k]);
//If a is a matrix, the notation a[m] picks out row m of that matrix

//partial pooling

for (n in 1:N)

//y_hat[n] <- a[condolist[n]] +beta[condolist[n]][1] * x[n,1]+beta[condolist[n]][2] * x[n,2]+beta[condolist[n]][3] * x[n,3];
y_hat[n] <- a[condolist[n]] +beta[1][condolist[n]] * x[n,1]+beta[2][condolist[n]] * x[n,2]+beta[3][condolist[n]] * x[n,3];

sigma_y ~ cauchy(0,2.5);
y ~ normal(y_hat, sigma_y);

}

generated quantities{
vector[N] y_tilde;
for (p in 1:N)
y_tilde[p] <- normal_rng(a[condolist[p]] +beta[1][condolist[p]] * x[p,1]+beta[2][condolist[p]] * x[p,2]+beta[3][condolist[p]] * x[p,3], sigma_y);

}

Did this model work OK?  It looks the right way around to
me in terms of the hierarchical model in that you're pooling
across the j in each column of beta.

You can vectorize this:

 for (j in 1:J)
    a[j]~ normal(0, sigma_a);

as just

  a ~ normal(0, sigma_a);

And you should be able to replace all those loops in mu_beta
with a single matrix multiply:

  mu_beta <- u * gamma;

As usual, don't trust my matrix algebra without confirming it
yourself!
